# M5 parity fixtures

`generate_rembg_u2net_fixture.py` generates the preprocessing/tensor parity
fixtures. `generate_python_ort_parity.py` is the separate level-2 real-ORT
generator. With Pillow 10.4.0
it reproduces the pinned `rembg` `BaseSession.normalize` preprocessing for
three licensed RGB fixtures at 3×2, 2×3 and 5×3 geometries. It stores decoded
RGB and complete 320×320 NCHW tensors as little-endian f32.

The checked-in `rust/` artifacts were generated by real CPU ONNX Runtime 1.23.2
using `models/m5_u2netp.toml`: complete Rust tensors, raw first-output tensors,
restored alpha, and raw straight-alpha RGBA cutouts (`.rgba`, with a separate
PNG artifact). `parity.json` is generated by comparing those files to Python
preprocessing; the three full tensors pass at max absolute error below 1e-6.
`python-ort-parity.json` records the pinned Python 3.12/Pillow 10.4.0/ORT
1.23.2 real-CPU output comparison (raw first output, restored alpha and
cutout), with narrow computed tolerances.
`python-ort-cloth-reference/` retains representative cloth logits, the
restored class-ID map, and all three category masks in the 0/255 binary
convention; the ignored Rust runtime test compares these values directly.

Regenerate the Python preprocessing side. The generator writes `parity.json`
itself; keep stdout separate so shell redirection cannot truncate that file:

```sh
PYTHONPATH=/private/tmp/m5-py312-pinned M5_RUST_ROOT=tests/fixtures/m5/rust \
  /opt/homebrew/bin/python3.12 tests/fixtures/m5/generate_rembg_u2net_fixture.py \
  > /private/tmp/m5-preprocessing-generation.log
```

Generate the level-2 Python ORT artifacts and computed parity report with the
development-only pinned environment (models are local and never downloaded):

```sh
PYTHONPATH=/private/tmp/m5-py312-pinned \
  M5_RUST_ROOT="$PWD/tests/fixtures/m5/rust" \
  M5_PARITY_REPORT="$PWD/tests/fixtures/m5/python-ort-parity.json" \
  /opt/homebrew/bin/python3.12 tests/fixtures/m5/generate_python_ort_parity.py
```
